About the school

Founded on one idea: understanding beats memorising.

Garments Public School opened in 2005 with three classrooms and a shared conviction — that children learn best when they're trusted to investigate, build, and get things wrong along the way. That conviction still shapes our timetable, our labs, and how our teachers plan a lesson.

Today we run a CBSE-aligned curriculum from Grade 1 through Grade 12, with dedicated tracks in the sciences, humanities, and commerce at senior secondary level, alongside sport, music, and design woven through every year.

On campus

Facilities students actually use daily

Every space on campus is built for a specific kind of work — not decoration, but the tools a subject needs to be taught properly.

Central Library

28,000 titles, a quiet reading hall, and a digital archive open through free periods.

Science Laboratories

Separate physics, chemistry, and biology labs equipped for individual student experiments.

Computer & Robotics Lab

Two labs covering programming, electronics, and a robotics club that competes regionally.

Sports Complex

Football field, athletics track, indoor courts, and a swimming pool with certified coaches.

Auditorium

700-seat hall for assemblies, the annual function, and inter-school competitions.

Art & Music Studio

Dedicated rooms for painting, ceramics, Indian classical vocals, and instrumental practice.

Cafeteria

Nutritionist-reviewed menus, with a separate allergy-safe counter for younger grades.

Transport

GPS-tracked buses covering 24 routes across the city, each with a staff attendant.

Curriculum

One school, three stages

Each stage has its own pace and focus, but all of them sit on the same foundation of inquiry-based teaching.

Foundation

Literacy & Numeracy

  • Phonics-based English and Hindi reading
  • Everyday-maths through games and manipulatives
  • Weekly library and storytelling sessions
Discovery

Environmental Studies

  • Garden-based science observations
  • Simple experiments in the junior lab
  • Term projects on local ecosystems
Expression

Art, Music & Movement

  • Daily physical education
  • Rotating art, craft, and music blocks
  • Annual house-level talent showcase
Core

Sciences & Mathematics

  • Introductory physics, chemistry, biology labs
  • Algebra, geometry, and data handling
  • Monthly Olympiad and quiz practice
Core

Languages & Humanities

  • English, Hindi, and a foreign language elective
  • History and civics through case studies
  • Debate and Model UN club
Applied

Technology & Design

  • Introductory coding and robotics
  • Design-thinking mini-projects
  • Inter-house science fair
Science stream

PCM / PCB

  • Board-aligned physics, chemistry, maths or biology
  • Weekly practical exams in dedicated labs
  • Career counselling for engineering and medicine
Commerce stream

Accounts, Business, Economics

  • Applied case studies with local businesses
  • Guest sessions with chartered accountants
  • Annual stock-market simulation
Humanities stream

History, Political Science, Psychology

  • Research-led seminar format in Grade 11–12
  • Published student journal each semester
  • Preparation for law and civil-services entrances

Admissions 2027–28

How admission works

Four steps, usually completed within three to four weeks of your first enquiry.

1

Enquire

Submit the enquiry form or call the admissions desk with your child's grade and age.

2

Campus visit

Tour the classrooms and labs, and meet the grade coordinator for that stage.

3

Assessment

An age-appropriate reading, maths, and interaction session — not a pass/fail exam.

4

Enrollment

Confirm the seat, submit documents, and receive the orientation pack.

Come see the campus

The admissions office is open Monday to Saturday. Tours run every day at 9:30am and 2:00pm — no appointment needed for a walk-through, though booking ahead means a coordinator can meet you.
